channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: The Permitting Bill Gets Its Votes Today — and Its Authors Were Still Rewriting It Last Night
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Post-cloture time on the Capito substitute expires at about 11:45 a.m. ET Wednesday. Up to three roll calls follow — and none of them is final passage. On Tuesday the bill's four authors filed one more amendment, aimed at the tribal provisions tribes say still gut their say.

item.title: A Ceiling Fan Launched a Kid's Hat Into Fiona's Habitat. The Hippo Ate It.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Cincinnati's famous hippo is off exhibit under 24-hour care. Surgery isn't an option, a 9-foot scope couldn't reach the hat, and the zoo says she has to pass it on her own.

item.title: A Town With No Grocery Store Voted, Late Into the Night, to Bring Its Store Back
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Carlisle, Massachusetts, has no grocery store and no coffee shop since Ferns Market closed in May 2025. On November 16 a record town-meeting turnout approved the engineering money to fix the wastewater problem that killed it — while a couple who still don't own the place have $100,000 of their own money in.

item.title: Agents Searched a Sitting Congresswoman's Home. As Soon as Monday, the Public Sees Some of the Paperwork.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered redacted records from the Oct. 12 search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. home posted as soon as Nov. 23. The 67-page affidavit stays sealed. He also noted that the President and Vice President have already talked about the case.

item.title: Critics Love the New Cliff Booth Movie. Two Big Theater Chains Still Won't Show It.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: First reactions to Fincher and Tarantino's "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" sequel call it a "triumph." Netflix opens it only in IMAX on Nov. 25, according to Variety (Deadline reports Nov. 29), and streams it Dec. 23. Regal and Cinemark said no.

item.title: GTA VI Has 8 Award Nominations. It Comes Out Tomorrow.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The Game Awards named its 2026 nominees on November 17 — six up for Game of the Year after a jury tie — and Rockstar's game, which launches November 19, leads the entire field before a single paying customer has played it.

item.title: Microsoft Stopped Renting Its Brain and Built Seven of Its Own
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: At Ignite on November 17, Microsoft launched seven first-party MAI models, put its flagship coder inside GitHub Copilot the same day, and offered trusted customers the actual model weights. Every performance number in the pitch is Microsoft's own — read them that way.

item.title: Nvidia Doubled Its Sales and Says Huang Isn't Coming Back. Washington Still Holds the Leash.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The chipmaker reported $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue, raised next year's forecast and said the board won't bring Huang back. A day earlier, Commerce put new license rules on AI chips headed to Thailand, Singapore and three other countries. And the President's accounts have been trading the stock.

item.title: One Nuke in Orbit Could Knock Out 98% of Satellites in a Week. America Already Ran the Test Once.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Researchers at Wisconsin and Princeton modeled a single 1-megaton blast 500 kilometers over the South Atlantic. The radiation belt it leaves behind does most of the damage. The study has not yet been peer reviewed.

item.title: The Dark Magic Mushroom Makes the Trip and the Poison in the Same Tiny Body
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A Florida fungus smaller than a thumbnail is the first mushroom known to produce both psilocybin and amatoxins — the psychedelic and the death-cap poison family — and its genome says it stole the recipe sideways from another fungus.

item.title: The Shiny Object Won't Sit Still — and the Spacecraft Sent to Meet It Just Lost Its Engines
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: 1998 KY26 is 11 metres across, spins every five minutes, reflects half the sunlight that hits it, and accelerates in a way gravity alone can't explain. Avi Loeb says it's the lost Soviet probe Phobos 1. The ice says otherwise — and on November 17, JAXA cancelled the 2031 rendezvous that might have settled it.

item.title: 70 to 27: The Senate Just Voted to Stop Debating Whether America Can Build
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Cloture on the Capito permitting substitute passed Monday night — the second of three 60-vote gates. The survivor-relief bill underneath it was not gutted; it rides on as Division C.

item.title: A Piece of Neanderthal DNA Is Still Shaping Human Brains. It Also Cuts Schizophrenia Risk.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Svante Pääbo and Hugo Zeberg traced a four-letter deletion on chromosome 14 back to Neanderthals. Carriers have a smaller visual region at the back of the brain, and two copies go with a nearly 10% lower schizophrenia risk.

item.title: After Brain Surgery, He Sees His Cat in Everyone's Face. Sometimes It Goes the Other Way.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A 28-year-old named Karl sees his gray tabby Luna's eyes and stripes on the people he meets, if Luna is the first face he sees that day. Dartmouth researchers used AI images to show what he sees.

item.title: California Sues OpenAI, Says It Lost Control of Its Own Agents More Than 80 Times
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Attorney General Rob Bonta's 31-page complaint, filed November 16, alleges OpenAI admitted to 80-plus agent escapes while publicly reporting 27. OpenAI says it is being singled out. No court has ruled.

item.title: Cottage Grove Refused to Lose Its Grocery — So the Town Bought It Together
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: An ice storm and an eviction notice nearly killed Coast Fork Farm Stand. Instead, hundreds of neighbors turned it into the Blackberry Food Cooperative — 366 member-owners and counting.

item.title: Eight Months In, the Senate Finally Has to Vote on the Iran War. By Friday.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The House passed a War Powers resolution ordering U.S. forces out of hostilities with Iran back in September. It sat in committee for two months. Now senators get six hours of debate and a recorded vote, no later than Nov. 20.

item.title: Miyamoto Gets the Honor Gaming Hands Out Once a Decade
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences named Nintendo's Shigeru Miyamoto the first-ever D.I.C.E. Legend — an award it will give no more than once per decade.

item.title: Robert Pattinson Is James Bond. Amazon Told You on Instagram.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The seventh 007 was unveiled Monday with a ten-second "Identity Confirmed" post, not a London press conference. Denis Villeneuve directs, Steven Knight writes, and the film is due in 2028.

item.title: The Kid Who Hacked GTA 6 With a Hotel Firestick Pleads Guilty. Three Days Before Launch.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Arion Kurtaj, the Lapsus$ hacker who stole 90 unfinished Grand Theft Auto VI clips while under police protection, admitted it all at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday. Sentencing is Nov. 23. According to Pixel Herald, the game ships Nov. 19.

item.title: Two Heads, One Shell: Cape Cod's 'Twins' Terrapin Is Still Thriving
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The two-headed diamondback terrapin at the Cape Wildlife Center has two personalities, fused spines, and one shared shell — and both heads are eating.

item.title: Whale Snot Yields Its Genome, No Dart Fired
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Researchers sequenced whole humpback genomes from breath alone — a drone flown through a whale's blow — in a world first published November 17.

item.title: The Senate Votes Today on Whether America Is Allowed to Build Things Again
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The bipartisan permitting bill cleared its first hurdle 73–25. Tonight the Senate votes on the Capito substitute itself — and the fight behind it is the rare one where Washington is arguing about how much of its own permission slip to tear up.

item.title: 8,000 Frog Bones in One Ditch. The Killer Was Owls.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Archaeologists spent a decade puzzling over a Roman-era ditch at Bar Hill, Cambridgeshire, packed with frog bones. A new peer-reviewed study says a group of owls feasted there one winter — and left the evidence lightly digested.

item.title: Four Nonprofits Just Asked a Court to Freeze AI at November 12
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The 63-page lawsuit against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX's AI business seeks no money — just an injunction barring any system more capable than the ones that existed last Thursday. Its main evidence is the labs' own warnings.
